fig1_position_momentum_tradeoff.svg: Two minimum-uncertainty Gaussians ($\hbar=m=1$): position densities $|\Psi(x)|^2$ (top) and their FFT momentum densities $|\tilde\Psi(p)|^2$ (bottom), with $\sigma_x,\sigma_p$ from the module's sigma_x/sigma_p. The narrow packet ($\sigma_x=0.7$) is broad in $p$ and the wide one ($\sigma_x=1.8$) is sharp in $p$, yet BOTH saturate $\sigma_x\sigma_p=\hbar/2$ — the trade-off is a property of the state.
fig2_ehrenfest_harmonic.svg: A coherent Gaussian ($x_0=3,\,\sigma=1$) evolved in $V=\frac12\omega^2x^2$ by the module's split_step_evolve. The recorded $\langle x\rangle(t)$ (blue) and $\langle p\rangle(t)$ (steel) obey $d\langle x\rangle/dt=\langle p\rangle/m$, and $\langle x\rangle$ lands exactly on the independent classical curve classical_sho (dots) — Ehrenfest's theorem is EXACT for the harmonic well, where $\langle V'(x)\rangle=V'(\langle x\rangle)$.
